It can fail when preserved large bins never receive a fitting large item, wasting capacity tight packing would have used.

Triangular peak at twice the item size: score falls with the absolute distance between a bin's residual and 2*item, so the preferred bin is the one that leaves exactly one item-sized gap after placement, keeping a same-size slot open. It can fail when item sizes vary widely, since the reserved gap rarely matches the next item and tight packing would have saved bins.

strategy: Mean-targeted distribution preference: score falls with the distance between a bin's residual and the mean of all currently feasible residuals, so the item goes to the most typical bin while unusually tight and unusually large bins are both preserved. It can fail when the mean is skewed by one huge bin, pulling items into mediocre middle bins.

Item-parity gate: even-sized items use tightest fit while odd-sized items use worst fit, preferring the largest residual; this separates the two parity classes into different bin pools, so odd items stop consuming the tight bins even items pack well into. strategy: Largest-bin shield: score by tightest fit but subtract a large penalty from the single largest feasible bin whenever another bin exists, so the roomiest bin is preserved for a future item that only it can fit. It can fail when the shielded bin is never needed and tight bins get overused instead.

Small-item worst fit: when the item is at most half the smallest feasible residual, score by largest residual, otherwise by tightest fit; small items are spread into roomy bins so tight bins stay free for large items that need them.
